# Secret-value shapes for scripts/secret-dump-compare.py (cadence-hooks#1662).
# Every row starts with a class and a space:
#   P  the value lands in the command's own output (may move ASK or ALLOW -> BLOCK)
#   C  the value goes to a consumer (must not move)
#   Q  nothing reaches the output, or no value is read (must not move)
#   L  stated limit: a later or remote command the guard does not read prints
#      the value; an under-block kept on purpose (must not move)
#   T  a filter after a value that selects no value, blocked on purpose by the
#      taint rule, which never reads filter text: `T <command> ## <reason>`
#      (may move ASK or ALLOW -> BLOCK; must block on head)
#   A  an accepted move on an everyday row: `A <command> ## <one-line reason>`.
#      An everyday row that moves without an A line fails the run.
# Item names and references are made up. Blank lines and `#` lines are skipped.
# A `⏎` in a row is a newline, so a row can hold a heredoc.
# The everyday rows come from scripts/testdata/confirm-tier-commands.txt.

# --- printed: the tool's own output ---
P op read op://v/i/f
P op read "op://v/item name/credential"
P op read op://v/i/f >&2
P op read op://v/i/f > /dev/stdout
P op read op://v/i/f -o /dev/stdout
P op read op://v/i/f 2>/dev/null
P op read --no-newline op://v/i/f
P op item get db --fields password --reveal
P op item get db --reveal --format json
P security find-generic-password -s svc -a me -w
P security find-generic-password -ws svc
P security find-internet-password -s host -w
P sudo security find-generic-password -s svc -w
P echo start; security find-generic-password -s x -w && echo done
P cd /repo && op read op://v/i/f
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}'
P kubectl -n prod get secrets/app -ojsonpath={.data.k}
P kubectl get secret s --template='{{.data.p}}'
P vault kv get -field=password secret/x
P vault read -field=value secret/x
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString --output text
P aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1
P aws ssm get-parameter --name /x --with-decryption
P aws configure get aws_secret_access_key
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v -n x
C az account get-access-token
P gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=x
P gcloud auth print-access-token
P heroku auth:token
P pass show x
P pass db
P gopass show db
P bw get password item
P lpass show --password item
P doppler secrets get KEY --plain

# --- printed: a substitution an argument printer prints, or a script ---
P echo $(op read op://v/i/f)
P echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P echo -n "token: $(op read op://v/i/f)"
P printf "%s\n" "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P echo `pass show x`
P sudo echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P sh -c 'pass show x'
P bash -c 'op read op://v/i/f'
P eval 'vault kv get -field=p secret/x'
P bash -c 'echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)"'

# --- consumer: a pipe into another program ---
C op read op://v/i/token | gh auth login --with-token
C op read op://v/i/f | docker login -u me --password-stdin registry.example
C security find-generic-password -s svc -w | docker login -u me --password-stdin
C security find-generic-password -s svc -w | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | tr -d '\n' | pbcopy
C op read op://v/i/f | wc -c
C op read op://v/i/f | grep -q expected
Q op read op://v/i/f | base64 -d > key.bin
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d
P kubectl get secret s -o json | jq -r .data.p | base64 -d
C bash -c 'op read op://v/i/f' | pbcopy

# --- consumer: a substitution used as an argument, assignment or prefix ---
L X=$(security find-generic-password -s svc -w); echo $X
C export GH_TOKEN="$(op read op://v/i/t)"
C GH_TOKEN="$(op read op://v/i/t)" gh api user
C TOKEN=$(op read op://v/i/f) gh api user
C env T="$(op read op://v/i/f)" npm publish
C curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $(op read op://v/i/f)" https://api.example
C curl -fsS -u "me:$(security find-generic-password -s svc -w)" https://api.example
C psql "postgres://u:$(pass show db)@h/db"
C mysql -p"$(pass show db)" -e 'select 1'
L ssh h "echo $(op read op://v/i/f)"
C gh secret set API_KEY --body "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C docker login --password-stdin <<< "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C gh auth login --with-token < <(op read op://v/i/f)
P cat <(pass show x)
C echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)" | docker login --password-stdin
Q echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)" > token.txt
Q echo $(op read op://v/i/f | sha256sum)
C $HOME/bin/tool --token "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C "$TOOL" login -p "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C ${KUBECTL:-kubectl} create secret generic s --from-literal=p="$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C printf -v TOKEN '%s' "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
Q echo hi 2>"$(op read op://v/i/f)"
Q echo <(op read op://v/i/f)
C docker login -u me --password-stdin <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C cat <<EOF | docker login --password-stdin⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C kubectl apply -f - <<EOF⏎kind: Secret⏎  pw: $(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
Q cat > config.yml <<EOF⏎pw: $(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
C psql <<-EOF⏎ALTER ROLE u PASSWORD '$(pass show db)';⏎EOF
C gh secret set K <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
P cat <<EOF⏎$(op read op://v/i/f)⏎EOF
Q echo "T=$(op read op://v/i/f)">>.env
Q printf '%s' "$(op read op://v/i/f)">.env
Q op read op://v/i/f>token.txt
Q op read op://v/i/f>/dev/null
Q op read op://v/i/f 2>&1>/dev/null
P op read op://v/i/f | tee .env
Q { op read op://v/i/f; } > token.txt
C ( op read op://v/i/f ) | pbcopy

# --- quiet: the value goes to a file or a hash, or nothing is read ---
Q op read op://v/i/f > token.txt
Q op read --out-file token.txt op://v/i/f
Q op read -o token.txt op://v/i/f
Q op read op://v/i/f | sha256sum
Q security find-generic-password -s svc -w | shasum -a 256
Q security find-generic-password -s svc -w > /dev/null
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d | shasum
Q op run --env-file app.env -- npm test
Q op run -- gh api user
Q op inject -i config.tpl -o config.yml
Q op item get db --fields username
Q op item get "Example Token" --fields label=token
Q op item list --vault Example
Q op vault list
Q op whoami
Q op signin
Q security find-generic-password -s svc
Q security unlock-keychain
P kubectl get secret app -o yaml
Q kubectl get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
Q vault kv get secret/x
Q aws configure get region
Q pass ls
Q echo 'op read op://v/i/f'
Q git commit -m 'op read op://x'
Q rg 'op read' src

# --- review round 1 (cadence-hooks#1663) ---
# A pipeline whose later stages all pass the value through prints it.
P op read op://v/i/f | cat
P op read op://v/i/f | tee
P op read op://v/i/f | head -c 10
P op read op://v/i/f | jq .
P op read op://v/i/f | xxd
P op read op://v/i/f | od -c
P cat <<< "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P echo "$(op read op://v/i/f)" | cat
# Printed forms main passed silently.
P op inject -i config.tpl
P perl -e 'alarm 9; exec @ARGV' op read op://v/i/f
P print -r -- "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
P az account get-access-token --query accessToken -o tsv
# A clipboard flag sends the value to the clipboard.
C pass -c db
C pass show -c db
C pass show --clip db
C pass -c2 db
C gopass show -c db
C lpass show -c --password item
# Default JSON whose value field the redactor masks.
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x
# Consumers behind the new forms keep main's verdict.
C op inject -i config.tpl | kubectl apply -f -
C perl -e 'alarm 9; exec @ARGV' op read op://v/i/f | pbcopy
C print -v T "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C op read op://v/i/f | tr -d '\n' | pbcopy
# Stdout closed, or sent after a stderr already in a file.
Q op read op://v/i/f >&-
Q op read op://v/i/f 1>&-
Q op read op://v/i/f 2>/dev/null >&2
Q op inject -i config.tpl > config.yml

# --- review round 1, second pass (code and security review of the delta) ---
P echo "$(op read "op://v/i/f")"
P printf '%s' "$(op read "op://v/i name/credential")"
P cat <<< "$(op read "op://v/i/f")"
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .SecretString
P az account get-access-token | jq -r .accessToken
P az account get-access-token -otsv
P op read op://v/i/f | jq -r .password
P op read op://v/i/f | sed 's/a/b/'
P op read op://v/i/f | head -n 1
P op read op://v/i/f | cut -c1-4
P op read op://v/i/f | tee /dev/tty | docker login --password-stdin
P kubectl get secret s -o json | jq -r '.data.token' | base64 -d
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq .
C print -rv T "$(op read op://v/i/f)"
C gopass show -co db
P pass show x | tail -n +2
P pass show x | sed -n 2p
T op read op://v/i/notes | jq keys ## the filter is not read; a jq stage after `op read` keeps the value
T op read op://v/i/notes | jq length ## the filter is not read; a jq stage after `op read` keeps the value
Q op read op://v/i/f | jq . other.json
Q op read op://v/i/f | cat /dev/null
Q op read op://v/i/f | xxd - out.hex
Q op read op://v/i/f | base64 -i in.txt
Q op read op://v/i/f | sed -ni 's/x/y/p' f
Q op read op://v/i/f >&out.txt
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items[].metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
P kubectl get secret s -o json | jq .
T kubectl get secret s -o yaml | yq '.metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
Q op inject --help
Q op read --help

# --- review round 2: selectors, help, queries and formats that print no value ---
Q kubectl get secrets -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'
Q kubectl get secrets -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.type}'
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations}'
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.metadata.creationTimestamp}'
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath="{.metadata.labels['app\.kubernetes\.io/name']}"
Q kubectl get secrets -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name
Q kubectl get secrets -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.type
Q kubectl get secrets -n prod -o go-template='{{range .items}}{{.metadata.name}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
Q az keyvault secret show --help
Q az keyvault secret show -h
Q gcloud secrets versions access --help
Q gcloud auth print-access-token --help
Q heroku auth:token --help
Q bw get password --help
Q gopass show --help
Q pass show --help
Q pass --version
Q az keyvault secret show --vault-name v --name n --query id -o tsv
Q az keyvault secret show --vault-name v --name n --query attributes.expires -o tsv
Q aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query Name --output text
Q aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query VersionId
Q aws ssm get-parameter --name /x --with-decryption --query Parameter.Version
Q az account get-access-token --query expiresOn -o tsv
Q az account get-access-token -o none
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --output yaml
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --output yaml-stream
C az account get-access-token -o yaml
C az account get-access-token -o jsonc
Q kubectl describe secret app
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | keys[]' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.data | length' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
C kubectl get secret app -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
Q kubectl get secret app -o yaml > secret.yaml
# A Secret's data reaching the output: no redactor test proves it masked.
P kubectl get secret app -o json
P kubectl get secrets -o yaml
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | map_values(@base64d)'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | to_entries[] | "\(.key)=\(.value | @base64d)"'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | .token' | base64 -d
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.["data"]["token"]' | base64 -d
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data'
P kubectl get secret app -o yaml | yq '.data'
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data}'
P kubectl get secret app -o go-template='{{range $k, $v := .data}}{{$k}}={{$v}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
# An output-format variable before the command selects the unmasked form.
P AWS_DEFAULT_OUTPUT=text aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x
P AZURE_CORE_OUTPUT=tsv az account get-access-token
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | tail -c 60
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString --output json
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v --name n --query value -o tsv

# --- review round 2, second pass (code and security review of the delta) ---
T kubectl get secrets -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | [.metadata.namespace, .metadata.name] | @tsv' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | keys | .[]' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data | to_entries[] | .key' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[0].metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq 'del(.data, .metadata.annotations)' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret s -o yaml | yq -o json '.metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret s -o json | jq --arg k v '.data | keys' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.database}'
T aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .ARN ## the filter is not read; `--query ARN` picks the field at the producer
T az account get-access-token | jq -r .expiresOn ## the filter is not read; `--query expiresOn` picks the field at the producer
Q aws ssm get-parameters-by-path --path /x --with-decryption --query 'Parameters[*].Name'
T op item get x --reveal --format json | jq -r '.fields[] | .label' ## the filter is not read; `op item get` without `--reveal` lists the labels
Q op read op://v/i/f >& out.txt
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.metadata.name + "=\(.data.token)"'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.annotations'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq 'del(.data)'
P kubectl get secret s -o jsonpath='{..password}'
P kubectl get secrets -o jsonpath='{.items[0]}'
P aws ssm get-parameters --names x --with-decryption --query 'Parameters[0]'
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query '*'
P pass show version

# --- review round 3: the taint rule (every jq/yq stage after a value keeps it) ---
# Finding 1: a field step after the value is already selected.
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString --output text | jq -r .password
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString --output text | jq -r .db.password
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x --query SecretString | jq -r 'fromjson | .password'
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .SecretString | jq -r .password
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v -n n --query value -o tsv | jq -r .password
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v -n n --query value -o tsv | jq -r .clientSecret
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r '.[]'
P aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq '..'
P az account get-access-token | jq -r '.[3]'
P az keyvault secret show --vault-name v -n n | jq -r '.[]'
P aws ssm get-parameter --name /x --with-decryption | jq -r '.Parameter | .[]'
P aws ssm get-parameters --names x --with-decryption | jq -r '.Parameters | .[0]'
P op item get db --reveal --format json | jq -r '.fields[1]'
P op item get db --reveal --format json | jq -r '.fields[]'
# Finding 2: filters that return their whole input, on a Secret.
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.name=="app")'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.type=="kubernetes.io/tls")'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | startswith("app"))'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq --arg n app '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == $n)'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels.app == "web")]'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items | map(select(.type == "Opaque"))'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items | sort_by(.metadata.creationTimestamp)'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items | group_by(.type)'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq 'first(.items[] | select(.type=="Opaque"))'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq 'if .type == "Opaque" then . else empty end'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.name, .'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.name, getpath(["data","token"])'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.name, (.|tojson)'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '{name: .metadata.name, data}'
P kubectl get secret app -o json | jq 'with_entries(select(.key != "kind"))'
P kubectl get secrets -o json | jq 'del(.data, .metadata.annotations)'
P kubectl get secrets -o yaml | yq '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "app")'
# Finding 3: a jsonpath that reaches data, into a decode filter.
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq 'map_values(@base64d)'
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq -r 'to_entries[] | "\(.key)=\(.value | @base64d)"'
P kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data}' | yq '.token'
# Name-listing filters the taint rule blocks on purpose (code review nits).
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata | .name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items[].metadata | {name, namespace}' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name | ascii_downcase' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name | select(startswith("a"))' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq '.items | group_by(.type) | map({type: .[0].type, n: length})' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.data | to_entries | map(.key)' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; `kubectl describe secret` lists the key names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata | .name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.creationTimestamp | fromdate' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; a jsonpath on `.metadata.creationTimestamp` reads it
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.resourceVersion | tonumber' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; a jsonpath on `.metadata.resourceVersion` reads it
T kubectl get secrets -o json | jq -r '.items[] | .metadata.name + " " + (.data | keys | join(","))' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; `kubectl describe secret` lists the key names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.data | has("token")' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; `kubectl describe secret` lists the key names
T kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.metadata.name' ## a filter on a Secret's json or yaml is not read; kubectl's own selector (`-o name`, a metadata jsonpath) lists names
T aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .Name ## the filter is not read; `--query Name` picks the field at the producer
# The ways to list names, and consumers and files after a filter, keep main's verdict.
Q kubectl get secrets -o name
Q kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'
Q kubectl get secrets -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
Q kubectl get secrets -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,TYPE:.type
Q kubectl describe secret app
Q op read op://v/i/f | jq -r .a > out.json
Q kubectl get secret app -o json | jq '.metadata.name' > names.txt
Q aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .SecretString | shasum
C kubectl get secret app -o json | jq -r '.data.token' | docker login --password-stdin u
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq -r .SecretString | pbcopy
C kubectl get secret app -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq -r .token | xargs -0 tool
C op read op://v/i/f | jq -f filter.jq data.json
P op read op://v/i/f | jq -f filter.jq
P op read op://v/i/f | yq -I 2 '.a'
P kubectl get -n prod secrets -o json
# A namespace or object named `secret` is not the Secret resource type.
Q kubectl get pods -n secrets -o yaml
Q kubectl get deploy secret -o json
# `jq .` after a masked cloud read keeps its ask only with options that keep the key names.
C aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id x | jq --arg a b .
C az account get-access-token | jq -c --indent 0 .
